Featured Project 01 • Quantitative Risk Management & Cloud AI

Dynamic Portfolio Optimization & Tail-Risk Stress Testing (Tadawul)

Enterprise FinTech & Risk Analytics Pipeline

Automated Portfolio Stress Testing & Generative AI Executive Reporting for Saudi Equities

Tech Stack: Python (SciPy, NumPy, Pandas), AWS S3, Amazon QuickSight, AWS Bedrock (Amazon Nova Lite LLM), Power BI

1. Business Challenge & Executive Summary

Conventional portfolio allocation models assume stable market correlations and normal return distributions, causing financial institutions to severely underestimate extreme downside exposure during macroeconomic or geopolitical shocks. This project engineers an automated, end-to-end risk management and cloud business intelligence solution for a 1,000,000 SAR institutional portfolio across four major Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) equities: Al Rajhi Bank (Financials), SABIC (Materials), Saudi Aramco (Energy), and STC (Telecommunications).

2. End-to-End Technical Architecture

Stage 01 • Data Pipeline
Market Parameterization

Ingested historical daily closing prices for Al Rajhi, SABIC, Aramco, and STC in Python to evaluate cross-asset correlations and empirically verify fat-tailed return behavior.

Stage 02 • Optimization
Constrained Allocation

Executed Sequential Least Squares Programming (SLSQP) in SciPy to determine optimal long-only capital weights that minimize portfolio volatility under baseline and stressed regimes.

Stage 03 • Stress Engine
10,000-Pathway Simulation

Simulated 10,000 independent 1-year terminal wealth trajectories to quantify 95% Value at Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR / Expected Shortfall).

Stage 04 • Cloud BI & GenAI
AWS QuickSight & Bedrock

Streamed simulation outputs to AWS S3 and Amazon QuickSight SPICE dashboards, triggering AWS Bedrock (Nova Lite LLM) to auto-generate executive risk memorandums.

Cross-Asset Correlation Matrix (left) and Empirical Daily Return Distributions (right) confirming fat-tailed market behavior across Tadawul equities.

3. Key Risk Insights & Interactive Executive Dashboard

Under normal market conditions, the optimization engine balances capital across STC (55%) and Al Rajhi Bank (45%). However, under simulated geopolitical stress, asset correlations break down and force a strict Corner Solution (100% concentration in Al Rajhi Bank). Simultaneously, the terminal wealth distribution shifts sharply leftward with severe negative skewness—demonstrating why standard VaR understates crisis exposure and why Expected Shortfall (CVaR) is essential for institutional capital adequacy.

Simulated 1-Year Portfolio Terminal Wealth Distribution (10,000 runs) contrasting the symmetric Baseline Scenario against the negatively skewed Geopolitical Shock Scenario.
Executive Risk Dashboard in Amazon QuickSight displaying comparative Monte Carlo wealth distributions, pre- and post-shock Markowitz portfolio weights, and automated VaR/CVaR severity cards.

4. Automated Executive Reporting via AWS Bedrock Generative AI

To eliminate manual reporting bottlenecks, the Python pipeline invokes the AWS Bedrock Converse API (amazon.nova-lite-v1:0) to translate raw simulation arrays directly into an actionable C-suite Risk Memorandum:

AWS Bedrock Automated Output • Executive Risk Memorandum

Subject: Stochastic Stress Test Results for Tadawul Portfolio
Following the completion of a comprehensive stochastic stress test utilizing 10,000 Monte Carlo pathways, it has been determined that the optimization algorithm has converged to a 100% allocation in Al Rajhi. Meanwhile, the 95% Value at Risk (VaR) has escalated from 134,767.66 SAR in the baseline exposure to 497,572.59 SAR under stress conditions (a 269.21% increase), and the Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) has surged from 184,175.18 SAR to 555,235.32 SAR (a 201.47% rise). In light of these findings, it is imperative to consider strategic diversification and tail-risk hedging to mitigate concentration exposure during stressed market regimes.

Featured Project 02 • Financial Forecasting & Time-Series Analytics

Multi-Decade Revenue Forecasting & Seasonal Time-Series Modeling (Coca-Cola)

Corporate Financial Planning & Predictive Forecasting

Quarterly Revenue Time-Series Analysis & 2-Year SARIMA Forecasting (1993–2026)

Tech Stack: R Statistical Environment (forecast, tseries, lmtest, ggplot2) • Dataset: Coca-Cola Corporate Financial Reports (1993 Q1 – 2024 Q1)

1. Business Objective & Dataset Profile

Accurate multi-quarter revenue forecasting is critical for corporate treasury planning, inventory allocation, and investor guidance. This project analyzes over three decades of quarterly revenue data for The Coca-Cola Company (spanning 1993 Q1 to 2024 Q1, 4 quarters per year, zero missing values) compiled from official financial reports to model long-term secular growth, isolate recurring quarterly seasonality, and generate a validated two-year revenue forecast with 80% and 95% confidence bounds.

Historical Horizon
1993 Q1 – 2024 Q1
125+ Quarterly Observations
Historical Revenue Range
$3,056M – $13,085M
Mean: $7,711M (SD: $2,859M)
Selected Forecasting Engine
Quarterly SARIMA
MLE Parameter p < 2.2e-16
Peak Projected Revenue (2026)
$13,417.05M
Projected in 2026 Q2

2. Analytical Workflow & Model Engineering

Step 01 • Exploration
Trend & Seasonality Profiling

Identified a strong multi-decade upward revenue trajectory alongside consistent quarterly seasonal cycles peaking in Q2/Q3.

Step 02 • Stabilization
Box-Cox & Differencing

Verified variance stability via Box-Cox diagnostic (0.86, confirming no non-linear transformation needed) and applied differencing to achieve mean stationarity.

Step 03 • Estimation
Quarterly SARIMA Fitting

Analyzed ACF/PACF lag spikes to fit a 4-quarter seasonal ARIMA architecture via Maximum Likelihood Estimation (estimate: -0.7876, p < 0.0001).

Step 04 • Validation
White-Noise Diagnostics

Validated model adequacy via Ljung-Box tests, residual ACF bounds, and one-sample t-test (p = 0.8933), confirming zero-mean white-noise residuals.

Historical Coca-Cola Quarterly Revenue (1993–2024) illustrating multi-decade expansion and pronounced quarterly seasonal cycles.
Two-Year Quarterly Revenue Forecast (blue trajectory) with 80% and 95% prediction intervals, projecting continued revenue growth.

3. Two-Year Quarterly Revenue Forecast & Confidence Bounds

The validated seasonal time-series model was deployed to project quarterly revenues across an 8-quarter forward horizon. The forecast captures Coca-Cola's signature Q2/Q3 summer demand peaks followed by Q4/Q1 moderation, projecting overall top-line expansion through 2026:

Featured Project 03 • Predictive Count Modeling & Segmentation

Demographic & Socioeconomic Count Modeling in R

Predictive Analytics & Behavioral Segmentation

Modeling Demographic & Tier Drivers of Household Group Size Using Poisson GLM

Tech Stack: R Statistical Environment (stats, ggplot2) • Methodology: Generalized Linear Modeling, Multiplicative Rate Ratios & Dispersion Diagnostics

1. Business Problem & Analytical Approach

In insurance underwriting, travel analytics, and customer segmentation, key behavioral metrics—such as accompanying family members, dependent counts, or event frequencies—are discrete, non-negative, and heavily right-skewed. Standard linear regression fails on skewed count data and produces invalid negative predictions.

This project applies a Poisson Generalized Linear Model (GLM) in R to quantify how customer Age and Service Tier (1st, 2nd, and 3rd Class) drive accompanying family group size (SibSp) on a reproducible sample (n = 60).

2. Key Model Findings & Multiplicative Impact

The Poisson GLM achieved strong convergence (reducing Null Deviance from 83.91 to a Residual Deviance of 62.69, AIC = 122.37). Transforming the model estimates into multiplicative Rate Ratios provides direct, business-ready insights into demographic behavior:

Predictor Segment Multiplicative Rate Ratio Statistical Significance (p-value) 95% Confidence Interval Practical Business Interpretation
Baseline Segment (1st Class) 1.965x 0.1611 (Reference) [-0.3506, 1.5443] Baseline reference group for tier comparisons
Customer Age (Per +1 Year) 0.956x 0.000319 *** [-0.0703, -0.0209] Highly significant negative driver; younger segments travel in significantly larger family units
Tier 2 Segment (vs. Tier 1) 0.405x 0.1201 [-2.1196, 0.2102] 40.5% expected group size relative to 1st Class (holding age constant)
Tier 3 Segment (vs. Tier 1) 1.333x 0.4820 [-0.4803, 1.1428] 33.3% larger expected family group size relative to 1st Class

3. Model Validation & Segment Interaction Visuals

Dispersion & Fit Validation: Model reliability was verified by computing the Pearson dispersion ratio (1.273). Because this ratio is close to 1.0, the Poisson variance assumption is well-satisfied without requiring complex overdispersion adjustments. Furthermore, cross-segment interaction visuals reveal that age-related group size differences are sharpest within the 3rd Class tier.

Right-skewed discrete count distribution of accompanying family members, demonstrating the need for specialized count regression.
